source: Original (authored 2026-11-17, no calculator). f(x) = a cos(bx) + d with min (0, -5), max (pi/3, 3): f(x) = -4cos(3x) - 1 on [0, pi]; dashed g = f(x + pi/4). Modelled on AA_HL_2025_Nov_P2_TZ1 Q4.

parts.label: a
parts.description: Find a and d (a real, may be negative).
parts.notes: A1 for a = -4 (the graph starts at a minimum, so a < 0). A1 for d = -1. Bare values earn the marks. Wrong method: a = 4: A0.

parts.label: b
parts.description: Find b.
parts.notes: M1 for period = 2 x pi/3 = 2pi/3 (minimum to maximum is half a period). A1 for b = 3. A bare 3 earns M0A1. Wrong methods: b = 6 (pi/3 taken as the period): M0A0; b = 2/3: M1A0.

parts.label: c
parts.description: f(x) = p sin(b(x - q)) - 1 with p > 0: write down p, find the smallest positive q.
parts.notes: A1 for p = 4. M1 for any valid method linking the forms: sin(theta - pi/2) = -cos theta; sine maximum where 3(x - q) = pi/2 at x = pi/3; or upward crossing a quarter period before the maximum. A1 for q = pi/6. Wrong method: q = pi/2 (from 3x - pi/2 without factoring the 3): M1A0.

parts.label: d_i
parts.description: Write down an expression for g(x) (dashed graph = f translated pi/4 to the left).
parts.notes: A1. Wrong methods, A0: f(x - pi/4) (the graph moved left); -4cos(3x + pi/4) - 1.
parts.follow_through: FT from the candidate's a, b, d.

parts.label: d_ii
parts.description: Find the exact value of g(0).
parts.notes: M1 for substituting x = 0 into the candidate's g, e.g. -4cos(3pi/4) - 1. A1 for 2sqrt2 - 1.

source: Original (authored 2026-11-17, no calculator). sec theta = -4, pi < theta < 3pi/2; cos 105 deg by compound angle; sec(7pi/12) rationalised. Modelled on AA_HL_2021_May_P1_TZ1 Q6.

parts.label: a
parts.description: sec theta = -4, theta in quadrant III: find exact tan theta.
parts.notes: M1 for 1 + tan^2 = sec^2 (or cos = -1/4 then sin = -sqrt15/4). A1 for tan^2 theta = 15 (or both sin and cos). A1 for sqrt15 (positive in quadrant III). -sqrt15 or +/- sqrt15 as the final answer earns M1A1A0. A bare sqrt15 earns M0A1A1.

parts.label: b
parts.description: Find exact cosec theta.
parts.notes: M1 for sin theta = -sqrt(1 - 1/16) or 1 + cot^2 = cosec^2. A1 for -4/sqrt15 (negative: sine negative in quadrant III). A positive value earns M1A0.

parts.label: c
parts.description: By writing 105 = 60 + 45, find exact cos 105 deg.
parts.notes: M1 for cos60 cos45 - sin60 sin45. A1 for (sqrt2 - sqrt6)/4. Wrong methods: plus sign, giving (sqrt2 + sqrt6)/4 (= cos 15): M0A0; cos60 + cos45: M0A0.

parts.label: d
parts.description: Write 105 deg in radians; find sec(7pi/12) with a rational denominator.
parts.notes: A1 for 7pi/12. M1 for 4/(sqrt2 - sqrt6) multiplied by the conjugate. A1 for -sqrt2 - sqrt6. Wrong method: sec = 1/sin: M0A0.

source: Original (authored 2026-11-17, no calculator). cos 2x - 3 sin x - 2 = 0 on [0, 2pi]. Modelled on AA_HL_2021_May_P1_TZ2 Q2.

parts.label: a
parts.description: Show cos 2x - 3 sin x - 2 = 0 can be written 2sin^2 x + 3 sin x + 1 = 0.
parts.notes: M1 for substituting cos 2x = 1 - 2sin^2 x (other double-angle forms earn M1 only once converted to sine). A1 for a correct line before the given result, e.g. -2sin^2 x - 3 sin x - 1 = 0. Wrong method: cos 2x = 1 - 2 sin x: M0A0.

parts.label: b
parts.description: Solve for 0 <= x <= 2pi.
parts.notes: M1 for factorising (2 sin x + 1)(sin x + 1) or the quadratic formula. A1 for sin x = -1/2 and sin x = -1. A1 for each of 7pi/6, 11pi/6, 3pi/2. If extra values are given (pi/6, 5pi/6 from a sign error, or values outside the interval), deduct one A mark. Answers in degrees earn M1A1 and A0 for the values.
parts.follow_through: FT from the candidate's values of sin x.

source: Original (authored 2026-11-17, calculator, radians). Triangle ABC: AB = 10, AC = 7, angle ABC = 0.6 rad, BC = x: ambiguous case through the cosine-rule quadratic.

parts.label: a
parts.notes: M1 for the cosine rule 7^2 = 10^2 + x^2 - 2(10)(x)cos 0.6. A1 for a correct rearranged line before the given result.

parts.label: b
parts.description: Find the two possible values of x.
parts.tolerance: Accept 3 s.f. or the calculator display with an ellipsis; a value cut short with no ellipsis earns A0 (markscheme-spec 21).
parts.notes: A1 for each value. GDC solver accepted without working. Wrong method: degree mode gives 17.0 and 3.00: A0A0.

parts.label: c
parts.description: Find the two possible values of angle ACB.
parts.tolerance: Accept any value consistent with the candidate's own correctly-rounded intermediate values; note premature rounding as feedback rather than withholding the accuracy mark. Accept 3 s.f. or the calculator display with an ellipsis; a value cut short with no ellipsis earns A0 (markscheme-spec 21).
parts.notes: M1 for the sine rule sin C/10 = sin 0.6/7 (or cosine rule with each x). A1 for 0.938. A1 for pi - 0.938... = 2.20. Degrees (53.8, 126) earn M1A0A0. Giving only 0.938 earns M1A1A0.
parts.follow_through: FT from (b) if the cosine rule is used.

parts.label: d
parts.description: Find the difference between the areas of the two possible triangles.
parts.tolerance: Accept any value consistent with the candidate's own correctly-rounded intermediate values; note premature rounding as feedback rather than withholding the accuracy mark. Example: 23.4 from x = 12.4 and 4.12. Accept 3 s.f. or the calculator display with an ellipsis; a value cut short with no ellipsis earns A0 (markscheme-spec 21).
parts.notes: M1 for two correct area expressions subtracted. A1 for 23.4. Wrong method: the area of one triangle only: M0A0.

source: Original (authored 2026-11-17, calculator). f(x) = sin x + sqrt3 cos x = 2 sin(x + pi/3) on [0, 2pi]. Modelled on AA_HL_2025_Nov_P1_TZ1 Q8 and AA_HL_2024_Nov_P1 Q9.

parts.label: a
parts.description: By expanding sin(x + pi/3), show f(x) = 2 sin(x + pi/3).
parts.notes: M1 for the compound-angle expansion sin x cos(pi/3) + cos x sin(pi/3). A1 for substituting 1/2 and sqrt3/2 and reaching sin x + sqrt3 cos x.

parts.label: b
parts.description: Describe fully the transformations mapping y = sin x onto y = f(x).

expected.answer: translation pi/3 to the left; vertical stretch scale factor 2

parts.tolerance: Either order. A translation word with a vector (-pi/3, 0) earns the translation mark.
parts.notes: A1 for a horizontal translation of pi/3 to the left (type, direction, size). A1 for a vertical stretch with scale factor 2. 'Move' earns A0. A purely symbolic description earns at most 1 mark (markscheme-spec 19). Translation to the right: A0 for that transformation.

parts.label: c
parts.description: Write down the range of f.

parts.label: d
parts.description: Solve f(x) = 1, exact multiples of pi.
parts.notes: M1 for sin(x + pi/3) = 1/2. A1 for at least one correct value of x + pi/3 in [pi/3, 7pi/3] (5pi/6 or 13pi/6). A1 for pi/2. A1 for 11pi/6. If -pi/6 (outside the domain) is given as an answer, deduct one A mark. GDC decimals (1.57, 5.76) earn M1A1A0A0.

parts.label: e
parts.description: Find the x-intercepts of f and the area of R between them.
parts.tolerance: Accept 2.09 and 5.24 for the intercepts. A GDC integral is accepted.
parts.notes: A1 for both intercepts. M1 for an integral of f (or |f|) between the candidate's intercepts. A1 for 4. Accept -4 as the integral with area stated as 4.

source: Original (authored 2026-11-17, calculator, radians). Daylight N(t) = a sin(b(t - c)) + d, t days; NYC max 15.1 (t = 172), min 9.3 (t = 355); Palermo max 14.8, min 9.5; same b, c. Modelled on AA_HL_2024_May_P2_TZ1 Q10.

parts.label: a
parts.description: Find a and d.
parts.notes: A1 each. Bare values earn A1A1.

parts.label: b
parts.description: Find b and c.
parts.tolerance: Accept b = 0.0172; accept c = 81.25 (from the minimum).
parts.notes: A1 for b. M1 for (2pi/365)(172 - c) = pi/2 or equivalent. A1 for c = 80.75. Wrong method: c = 172 (the cosine shift): M0A0.

parts.label: c
parts.description: Find p and q.
parts.notes: A1 each.

parts.label: d
parts.description: Rate of change of daylight in New York at t = 321, in minutes per day.
parts.tolerance: Accept any value consistent with the candidate's own correctly-rounded intermediate values; note premature rounding as feedback rather than withholding the accuracy mark. Examples: -1.65 from c = 81.25; -1.64 from b = 0.0172. Accept 'decreasing at 1.63 minutes per day'. Accept 3 s.f. or the calculator display with an ellipsis; a value cut short with no ellipsis earns A0 (markscheme-spec 21).
parts.notes: M1 for N'(t) = ab cos(b(t - c)) or a GDC derivative at t = 321. A1 for -0.0272 hours per day. A1 for -1.63 minutes per day. Wrong method: degree mode gives +2.99: M1A0A0.

parts.label: e
parts.description: Number of days in the year on which Palermo has more daylight than New York.
parts.tolerance: Accept any value consistent with the candidate's own correctly-rounded intermediate values; note premature rounding as feedback rather than withholding the accuracy mark. Example: 159 (158.935...) from b = 0.0172. Accept 3 s.f. or the calculator display with an ellipsis; a value cut short with no ellipsis earns A0 (markscheme-spec 21).
parts.notes: M1 for P(t) = N(t) or a graph of P - N. A1 for t = 69.1 and t = 275. A1 for 365 - (274.947... - 69.0528...) = 159. Wrong method: 206 (the time New York has more daylight): M1A1A0.
